input.quote: 11.2 Indemnification of AbbVie. Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents (the "AbbVie Indemnitees"), and defend and save each of them harmless, from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]
input.rationale: A counterparty-side indemnity in our favour exists and is not one-way. Section 11.2 requires Harpoon to defend, indemnify and hold harmless AbbVie, its Affiliates and their directors, officers, employees and agents against Losses from Third Party Claims, and Sections 11.3–11.4 supply the standard procedure the playbook expects: prompt notice with no forfeiture for delay (p0561), indemnifying-party control of defence with reasonably acceptable counsel (p0564–p0565), our right to participate and to take control if Harpoon fails to assume the defence or interests are adverse (p0567), settlement only with our consent where non-monetary relief is involved (p0568), cooperation with expense reimbursement (p0570) and interim reimbursement of our defence costs (p0571). Third-party IP infringement exposure is captured: Section 7.4 addresses third-party patent infringement claims against AbbVie expressly "Subject to Section 11.2", and Section 11.4.1 is made subject to Sections 7.4/7.5/7.6, so the Harpoon indemnity is the backstop for those claims. Harpoon's indemnity is also carved out of the consequential-damages exclusion (p0572, limb (D)) and is not subject to any super-cap, which is better than the fallback. Two points noted rather than flagged: (i) the substantive triggers in both 11.1 and 11.2 are redacted ([***]) in this filed copy, so on execution we should confirm 11.2 expressly reaches IP infringement, Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law and its gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and that our reciprocal 11.1 indemnity is confined to AbbVie's own development/commercialisation conduct and breach of law; and (ii) this is a collaboration/licence rather than a services deal, so the reciprocal 11.1 indemnity reflects the ordinary licence bargain and is not a deviation. No redline proposed.
